engine: offline: the agent acted as the LLM designer (proposals, rationales, critiques); evaluation, ranking and selection are code

A.name: PROMETHEUS
A.title: Brain A · the Structuralist
A.creed: Intelligence is the discovery of structure: rules, programs, compositional abstractions.

B.name: SIBYL
B.title: Brain B · the Empiricist
B.creed: Intelligence is compressed experience: memory, statistics, prediction.

W.name: WILD CARD
W.title: Protected slot · radical ideas
W.creed: A slot for a paradigm nobody asked for. Protected as a slot, never from THE REAPER.

tasks.name: Addition
tasks.blurb: a + b with a, b in 0..4. Answer the digit of the sum.

tasks.name: Sequence continuation
tasks.blurb: a, a+d, a+2d (mod 10) with d in 1..3. What comes next?

tasks.name: Bigger number
tasks.blurb: Two different digits: is the left (L) or the right (R) one bigger?

tasks.name: Smallest divisor
tasks.blurb: A number 10..99 as two digits: its smallest divisor above 1 (2, 3, 5, 7, or P for a prime above 7).

tasks.name: Rock paper scissors (cycler)
tasks.blurb: The opponent cycles R → P → S. You see its last two moves: play the move that beats its next one.

tasks.name: Pick by position
tasks.blurb: Three letters A..F and a position 1..3: answer the letter at that position.

tasks.name: Subtraction
tasks.blurb: a − b with 0 ≤ b ≤ a ≤ 6.

tasks.name: Pattern completion
tasks.blurb: Four to seven letters repeating with period 2 or 3 (ABCAB, ABABAB…): the next letter.

tasks.name: 5-letter word
tasks.blurb: A common 5-letter word with one letter blanked (_). Any letter that makes a real word counts.

tasks.name: Simon memory
tasks.blurb: A sequence of 3 to 5 coloured lights then a query #k: which colour was light k?

tasks.name: Analogy
tasks.blurb: A is to B as C is to ? Letters A..H; the hidden rule is a shift by 1..3 (wrapping H→A).

tasks.name: Pong control
tasks.blurb: Ball row 0..7, its vertical direction U/D, your paddle row 0..7 and the ball's distance 1..4: move U, D or S(tay) toward where the ball will cross (it bounces off the walls).

tasks.name: Rock paper scissors (looper)
tasks.blurb: A new opponent loops R R P S S P … You see its last two moves: beat its next one.

tasks.name: Boolean logic
tasks.blurb: a OP b with bits a, b and OP one of & (and), | (or), ^ (xor).

tasks.name: Odd one out
tasks.blurb: Four letters, three the same: the position (1-4) of the odd one.

tasks.name: Grid path planning
tasks.blurb: On a 5×5 grid: you (x,y), the goal (x,y), a wall cell (x,y). Any first move on a shortest path that avoids the wall is right.

tasks.name: Ordering steps
tasks.blurb: Four numbered blocks in a row, not yet in order: where (1-3) does a bubble sort make its first swap?

tasks.name: Next word
tasks.blurb: A tiny language: subject + verb, then any object that fits the verb (eats fish/bread, reads book/map, drinks milk/tea).

tasks.name: Transitive inference
tasks.blurb: x beats y, y beats z (as three pairs of letters), then a query pair: does the first beat the second?

tasks.name: Key then door
tasks.blurb: A corridor 0..6: your cell, the key, the door, and whether you hold the key (Y/N). Step L or R toward the key first, then the door.

tasks.name: Counting
tasks.blurb: Five letters from A..C, then a query letter: how many times does it appear?

memory.label: Memory capacity
memory.desc: how much experience it may keep (episode store, rehearsal buffer, reservoir size)

depth.label: Abstraction depth
depth.desc: levels of abstraction (program depth, hidden width, similarity level)

compose.label: Compositionality
compose.desc: how freely parts combine (composed rules, pair features)

search.label: Search budget
search.desc: effort per trial (hypotheses kept, neighbours polled, replay steps, sim steps)

gate.label: Confidence gate
gate.desc: how sure it must be before it answers (THE REAPER charges −2 per wrong answer)

mechs.metacog: abstains unless its own track record is good
mechs.recode: reserved: not yet expressed by any paradigm (a neutral gene that copy errors can flip)

rule.name: Rule induction
rule.desc: searches a grammar of symbolic programs and keeps the ones the evidence supports

memory.name: Memory lookup
memory.desc: stores episodes and answers by recalling the most similar ones

nexttoken.name: Next-token predictor
nexttoken.desc: a transformer-lite trained online by backprop to predict the answer token

spiking.name: Spiking network
spiking.desc: leaky integrate-and-fire reservoir with reward-gated Hebbian readout

bayes.name: Bayesian structure averaging
bayes.desc: open-ended (LLM-proposed): averages Dirichlet models over context subsets by evidence

gp.name: Lifetime program evolution
gp.desc: open-ended (LLM-proposed): evolves expression trees inside one lifetime

relational.name: Relational recoder
relational.desc: open-ended (LLM-proposed): recodes tokens into roles, learns over role patterns

hybrid.name: Hybrid
hybrid.desc: two complete learners under a cascade or arbiter controller

gens.title: Genesis: five paradigms meet THE REAPER
gens.note: No seed yet. Each brain fields two genuinely different paradigms; the wild card is an open-ended design.

entries.name: Occam Engine
entries.rationale: A program that explains every observation is the most portable thing a learner can own. I enumerate a grammar of small programs (copy, shift, sum, difference, compare, extrapolate, pointer, small lookup tables), keep a soft version space, and answer only with the simplest program that has earned 80% trust. Depth 2 gives binary programs; pair tables give compositional rules for games. Expect: near-perfect on any task inside the grammar, silent (not wrong) outside it.
entries.critique: Dev 0.99, selection 0.35: the grammar mirrors the families it was written for. Outside the grammar the Engine is silent rather than wrong (good calibration), but silence scores nothing, and relabelled digits stop being numbers (transfer ratio 0.79).

entries.name: Synaptic Chorus
entries.rationale: A hedge against my own bias: no symbols at all. A leaky integrate-and-fire reservoir with reward-gated Hebbian readout, the Neuro Arena lineage. Structure should emerge in the synapses rather than in a grammar. Expect: slow, but no assumptions about what tokens mean.
entries.critique: Reached criterion on 2 of 24 streams. A random reservoir with a Hebbian readout needs more than 240 trials to carve out task structure, and the homeostatic gate kept it mostly silent. Honest result, not a tuned one.

entries.name: Mnemosyne
entries.rationale: Most of the world repeats. Keep every episode, answer from the exact match or a short nearest-neighbour vote, abstain unless the vote clears 70%. No inductive leap, so nothing to be wrong about: whatever generalization it has comes from the fact that small worlds recur.
entries.critique: It wins by recurrence: the small worlds (subtraction, logic, the looping opponent, block ordering) repeat within 240 trials, so lookup solves them, and memory is blind to what symbols look like (transfer ratio 1.09). It fails wherever every trial is new: Simon, word completion, grid planning.
entries.fate: passed on: seed of both brains

entries.name: Little Oracle
entries.rationale: The paradigm behind today's LLMs, shrunk to fit a trial: token + position embeddings, one attention head, tied output embeddings for copying, online cross-entropy with rehearsal, and a metacognitive gate. It should be the most general of all if it gets enough data; the risk is sample efficiency within 240 trials.
entries.critique: Transfers as well as memory (ratio 1.04) but needs a median of 108 trials to reach criterion. Sample efficiency, not capacity, is its bottleneck at this scale.

entries.name: Bayes Cathedral
entries.origin: offline LLM (agent) · wild card (open-ended, no template)
entries.rationale: Neither rules nor neurons: a probabilistic structure learner. Every subset of up to two input positions is a candidate model of the answer; models are averaged by their marginal likelihood, and the decision rule is the Bayes-optimal one for THE REAPER (answer iff p > 2/3). It discovers WHICH inputs matter instead of what the rule is.
entries.critique: Finds which positions matter, but averaging over pairs of positions is too coarse for tasks whose rule involves three tokens or none (Simon, analogy, grid).

verdict.text: B1 Memory lookup wins with REAPER 0.475 (S 0.49, Q 0.40, X 0.53), 0.126 ahead of A1.

gens.title: Reprogrammed: both brains start from Mnemosyne
gens.note: THE REAPER passed on B1 (memory lookup, seed) and A1 (rule induction, crossover partner). Both brains now build from the memory genome; the wild card brings a new paradigm.

entries.name: Structured Memory
ops: relational bias on: recall also by the sameness pattern, answers stored as "the token at position j"
abstraction depth 1→2: numeric closeness counts as partial similarity
entries.rationale: I lost to memory, so I take its genome and give it what my rules had: structure. A recalled answer should be stored as a ROLE ("the token at position 3"), not as a symbol, so it applies to inputs never seen before; and near-miss digits should count as near. This should help exactly where Mnemosyne failed: trials that never repeat.
entries.critique: Selection up from 0.475 to 0.504, mostly from faster solving. But its score on the sealed families fell from 0.27 to 0.11: recalling by the sameness pattern overcommits when a sealed family shares a pattern but not a rule. (Logged for the record; THE REAPER never sees the sealed set.)

entries.name: Chimera of the Fittest
entries.rationale: No LLM in this slot: the built-in crossover operator recombines the two genomes THE REAPER passed on.
entries.critique: The built-in crossover found what neither brain proposed: a cascade where memory answers trials it has seen and the rule engine answers the ones that have structure. Most streams solved (16/24) and fastest median (32 trials). Neither LLM designer gets the credit for this one.
entries.fate: passed on: seed of both brains

entries.name: Deep Archive
entries.rationale: My design won; do not fix what works. More capacity so nothing is forgotten in a lifetime, a wider vote so the neighbours average out noise, and a slightly stricter gate because a wrong answer costs twice a right one.
entries.critique: More capacity bought nothing in 240 trials, and the stricter gate slowed it down (speed 0.40→0.34). Exploitation without exploration.

entries.name: Copy-error Mnemosyne
entries.rationale: No LLM in this slot: random copy errors in the seed genome (genes moved by Gaussian noise, biases and mechanisms flipped).
entries.critique: Random copy errors were roughly neutral (+0.017).

entries.name: Relational Recoder
entries.origin: offline LLM (agent) · wild card (open-ended, no template)
entries.rationale: A paradigm nobody fielded: learn over ROLES instead of tokens. Each trial is recoded into its relational signature (which positions are the same, which are in order), the answer into an expression over the input (copy position j, position j plus c, or a literal), and the learner tracks which expression wins for each signature, backing off to coarser signatures. Built to be indifferent to relabelling.
entries.critique: Weak on the selection battery (0.27) but second best on the sealed families (0.44): roles transfer to transitive inference and counting. Suppressed by THE REAPER all the same, which is the rule: the wild card is protected as a slot, never from the score.

verdict.text: A2 Hybrid (cascade): Memory lookup + Rule induction wins with REAPER 0.529 (S 0.58, Q 0.50, X 0.51), 0.025 ahead of A1.

gens.title: The chimera seeds both brains
gens.note: THE REAPER passed on A2 (hybrid cascade memory → rule, built by the crossover operator) as the seed and A1 (structured memory) as the partner.

entries.name: Rules First
ops: cascade order reversed: a trusted program answers before memory
entries.rationale: A program that has been right 80% of the time should outrank a vote of neighbours: it generalizes to inputs memory has never seen. Put the rules first and let memory catch what the grammar cannot express.
entries.critique: Rules first scored 0.555, within 0.006 of the winner: on this battery the order of the cascade barely matters, because the two parts rarely both claim the same trial. It kept the best sealed score of the cascades.

entries.name: Second Crossing
entries.rationale: No LLM in this slot: built-in crossover of the two passed-on genomes, then light copy errors.
entries.critique: Second by 0.002. Its memory part inherited the relational recall from Structured Memory, which helps the scrambled streams (X 0.555) but, again, hurts the sealed families (0.29).

entries.name: Parliament
ops: controller cascade → arbiter: the part with the better running record answers
entries.rationale: A fixed order is a prejudice. Let the evidence decide per task: both parts keep a shadow record of what THE REAPER would have paid them, and the better record answers.
entries.critique: Won by 0.002, a margin well inside the noise of one battery: THE REAPER still has to pick one, and it does so by its score alone. The arbiter also has the best sealed score so far (0.52).
entries.fate: passed on: seed of both brains

entries.name: Copy-error Chimera
entries.rationale: No LLM in this slot: random copy errors in the seed genome, including inside both parts.
entries.critique: Copy errors cost 0.018; turning replay off has no effect on these parts (neither uses the replay mechanism), the rest was noise.

entries.name: Darwin in a Bottle
entries.origin: offline LLM (agent) · wild card (open-ended, no template)
entries.rationale: Evolution inside a lifetime: a population of arithmetic expression trees evolves every few trials on a buffer of recent episodes, and the fittest tree answers once it is accurate on that buffer. Evolution within evolution: the outer loop selects how the inner loop searches.
entries.critique: Its trees evolve over digit VALUES, so on scrambled streams, where digits become glyphs, it solved nothing (X = 0). Dev 0.64 hid that completely. The clearest case of surface dependence in the run.

verdict.text: B1 Hybrid (arbiter): Memory lookup + Rule induction wins with REAPER 0.561 (S 0.60, Q 0.53, X 0.56), 0.002 ahead of A2.

gens.title: Plateau: the brains reach for depth and breadth
gens.note: THE REAPER passed on B1 (arbiter memory + rule) as the seed and A2 (cascade with relational memory) as the partner. Three hybrids finished within 0.006 of each other: the population is converging, so the wild card resurrects a suppressed paradigm with a radically different genome.

entries.name: Deep Grammar
ops: rule part: abstraction depth 2→3 (ternary programs such as c + (b − a))
rule part: relational bias on (rules keyed by the sameness pattern; copy the position the pattern points to)
entries.rationale: The plateau is a grammar ceiling. Depth 3 lets the engine express analogies between pairs, and relational rules let it speak about positions and sameness instead of symbol values, which is the only thing that survives a scramble.
entries.critique: Depth 3 + relational rules gave the best plain score of the run (S 0.70) and the best sealed score (0.67): analogy 95%, oddone 93%, pattern 95%. Its scrambled analogy collapsed to 34% (ternary rules read digit values). It lost THE REAPER by 0.001, and the post-hoc audit on four fresh batteries says the order was luck: A1 averages 0.608, B2 0.592. Selection used one battery, as the rules say; the lesson is a bigger battery, not a different verdict.

entries.name: Third Crossing
entries.rationale: No LLM in this slot: built-in crossover of the two passed-on genomes, then light copy errors.
entries.critique: Crossover dragged in the partner's cascade and dropped temporal priors: pattern fell from 93% to 33%. A copy error can delete a capability in one step.

entries.name: Parliament + Oracle
entries.paradigm: Hybrid (arbiter): Hybrid (arbiter): Memory lookup + Rule induction + Next-token predictor
ops: the whole seed becomes part 1 of a new arbiter
part 2: a next-token predictor (the gen-1 Little Oracle genome) for what neither memory nor rules cover
entries.rationale: Memory covers what repeats, rules cover what is in the grammar; nothing covers the rest. A next-token predictor is slow, but it is the only part that can learn a mapping nobody wrote down, and the arbiter only lets it speak once its record is good.
entries.critique: Adding an Oracle as a third voice solved the most streams (19/24) and lifted grid planning from 21% to 45%, but the arbiter trusts it too early on nextword (0% plain): a new voice costs credibility before it earns it.

entries.name: Copy-error Parliament
entries.rationale: No LLM in this slot: random copy errors in the seed genome.
entries.critique: No designer touched this one: random copy errors (relational bias on in both parts, a looser gate) won by 0.001. It is a real improvement on the gen-3 seed (oddone 43%→95%) but its margin over A1 is inside battery noise (audit sd ≈ 0.01).
entries.fate: passed on: seed of both brains

entries.name: Lazarus Reservoir
entries.origin: offline LLM (agent) · wild card (heresy: a suppressed paradigm, radically re-genomed)
entries.rationale: Everything alive is now a memory-rule hybrid. The wild card resurrects the spiking network THE REAPER suppressed in generation 1, with a very different genome: 366 neurons, 16 steps, fast plasticity, wide fan-out, and input lines for sameness between tokens, so the reservoir can feel relations instead of symbols.
entries.critique: The resurrected reservoir found a niche nobody else holds: nextword 90% plain and 88% scrambled, the best of the run. Everywhere else it is near zero, so it is suppressed. A niche is not generalization.

verdict.text: B2 Hybrid (arbiter): Memory lookup + Rule induction wins with REAPER 0.639 (S 0.66, Q 0.66, X 0.60), 0.001 ahead of A1.
